messages:
incident-bot: ALERT severity=P1 · GPU queue growth detected for cluster-prod-gpu (metric: gpu_request_queue_length) > 120 for 5m. Autoscaler events showing repeated failures to add nodes. Paging oncall: @alice :rotating_light:
alice: Ack - I'm on it. Pulling dashboards now.
alice: Topline: queue spiked ~07:42 UTC, 3x normal. 429s to hosted/gpu-gen are increasing.
ben: On my way to standby. Any immediate customer impact? Which products?
alice: Mainly Dedicated inference and some Hosted customers with pinned GPU models. We are seeing throttling at the API layer as requests pile up.
maria: Looking at autoscaler logs: multiple `ScaleUp` attempts, then failures with AWS API errors.
simon: Paste of the most recent autoscaler error: ```W0506 07:49:32.123 node_group.go:244] AddNodeGroup GPU-pool-prod failed: create launch template: UnauthorizedOperation: You are not authorized to perform this operation\tstatus code: 403, request id: 1234-abc```
alice: Also seeing errors about taints on node group mismatch: pods cannot schedule because node taints don't match tolerations.
ben: Can someone `kubectl get pods -n redwood-system -o wide` and show Pending pods?
maria: ```NAME                      READY STATUS    RESTARTS AGE   NODE
gpu-infer-qtz-abcde        0/1   Pending   0       6m   <none>
Message: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taint {gpu: true}, that the pod didn't tolerate.```
kevin: That looks like the launch template the autoscaler is trying to use has `taints: gpu=true:NoSchedule` but our pod specs rely on `tolerations: gpu=true:PreferNoSchedule` (typo).
simon: Confirmed. Two problems: 1) IAM/launch-template API calls failing for a subset of nodegroups due to a recently changed IAM role, 2) taint/toleration mismatch for the new GPU nodegroup template.
alice: Impact assessment: ~18% of GPU requests are queued >15s; a handful of customers reported timeouts and increased latency. No data exfiltration. Priority: restore capacity.
ops-pager: Noted — alerting AWS infra on-call about IAM 403.
ben: Immediate mitigations: 1) enable fallback routing to CPU model variant for non-SLO traffic, 2) reduce burst window on hosted/gpu-gen route to limit queue growth, 3) try manual ASG scale for existing GPU nodegroup that still has working launch template.
maria: Attempting manual scale on older GPU ASG (gpu-asg-legacy): `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-asg-legacy --desired-capacity 6`
deploy-bot: Manual scale request queued - cloud API returned `RequestLimitExceeded` then `Throttling` for a few seconds, then success: desired=6.
maria: New nodes from legacy ASG came up but they're CPU-only—no GPUs. Some pods scheduled on them (not ideal).
ben: Can we temporarily modify serving config to allow CPU fallback for low-priority jobs?
alice: Yes, I'm patching the routing policy to route any request with metadata `priority: low` to `model-cpu-v2` and adding a notice to status page.
kevin: Small fix: I'll correct the pod toleration as an emergency patch in the model-deployment helm chart (change `PreferNoSchedule` -> `NoSchedule` to match taint) and push a canary.
simon: Wait - if we change toleration to `NoSchedule` they'll schedule on GPU nodes which is desired, but we also need the launch template fixed to avoid the IAM failure first.
ben: Who owns the IAM role used for launch templates?
kevin: That's `infra-node-launcher-prod-role`, modified yesterday by infra automation.
ops-pager: Infra on-call (aws-team) acknowledged and is rolling back the recent policy change. ETA ~15-25m.
alice: While infra fixes IAM, I'll continue routing reductions and increase retry window on the API client to avoid cascading failures. Also enabling autoscaler debug logs.
maria: Autoscaler debug shows the exact API call failing: `ec2:CreateLaunchTemplateVersion` returns AccessDenied for the node-launcher role.
ben: If infra can't fix quick: plan B = create a temporary manual GPU nodegroup with a confirmed-good launch template using an older role, and attach it to cluster. Anyone available to run infra CLI?
simon: I can create the nodegroup if infra approves, but that still requires IAM permissions.
kevin: For the taint mismatch I pushed a quick helm patch to add the missing toleration to the pod template for canary (image tag canary-toleration-fix). Applying now.
alice: Patch applied. One canary pod scheduled onto the newly created (legacy) gpu node but it's CPU-only so not helpful yet. Will re-evaluate after IAM rollback.
ben: Customer comms: I'll draft a short status update: "We are experiencing GPU capacity issues causing degraded latency for GPU-backed models. We're routing low-priority requests to CPU models while we restore GPU capacity. No data loss. Next update in 30m."
kevin: Infra rolled back the policy at 07:59 UTC and confirmed `iam:PassRole` restored for infra-node-launcher-prod-role.
maria: Re-running autoscaler scale attempt... ```I0506 08:01:12.987 scale_up.go:102] Attempting scale-up: node group GPU-pool-prod desired->+3```
simon: AWS responded: new launch template versions created, ASG launching GPU instances.
alice: New GPU nodes are registering. `kubectl get nodes` shows 3 new `p4d/p3` workers with taint `gpu=true:NoSchedule`.
kevin: The pods with corrected tolerations are scheduling onto new nodes. Queue length is dropping.
alice: Metrics: queued requests down to baseline within ~9 minutes of IAM rollback. Latency and 429s trending back to normal.
ops-pager: Good. Please confirm we have root cause and follow-up items.
ben: Root cause: recent IAM policy change removed permission needed for `CreateLaunchTemplateVersion`/`PassRole` for the node-launcher service account. Secondary issue: chart had a toleration typo `PreferNoSchedule` that prevented pods from accepting GPU tainted nodes.
alice: Action items (owners):
- infra: add a pre-deployment checklist entry for node-lifecycle IAM perms (ops-pager) — due EOD
- infra: audit and restore least-privilege role mapping; rollback guard rails (ops-pager) — due 24h
- platform: fix toleration in helm chart and add e2e scheduling test for GPU taints (kevin) — PR opened #4892
- runtime: add graceful CPU fallback for pinned GPU routes and flagging in metrics (maria) — follow-up ticket #2316
- SRE: add alert that separates "scale attempt failed due to IAM" from generic scale failures (alice) — PR to alerting repo
ben: Handoff: I'm going to be on-call for the next 45m and will track infra rollback/verification. If anything else crops up, ping me directly.
alice: Thanks team. Closing paging loop. I'll update the incident board and create the postmortem stub. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Incident resolved marker applied to thread 1760605123 at 1760608589
